introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics With Statistics, Paper 3 (0770/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Duration: THREE HOURS.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae and tables produced by the GCE Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Electronic calculators may be used. Start each question on a fresh page.

[The paper has 8 questions; the marks printed beside the parts add up to 13 for each question. No total is printed on the cover page.]
enonce_intro_markdown:
The lengths, to the nearest cm, of some randomly selected 140 leaves from a certain fruit tree were measured and recorded as follows:

| Length in cm | 5 - 9 | 10 - 14 | 15 - 19 | 20 - 24 | 25 - 29 | 30 - 34 | 35 - 39 | 40 - 44 | 45 - 49 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of leaves | 11 | 13 | 17 | 20 | 25 | 22 | 16 | 12 | 4 |

figures.legende: Cumulative frequency curve (ogive) of the 140 leaf lengths, with the quartiles read at cumulative frequencies 35 and 105 (model answer to Q2(c) and (d)).

incertitudes: Question 2 (b) : la moyenne et la variance sont calculées sur les centres de classe (7, 12, ..., 47) avec le diviseur $n = 140$ (variance de la distribution groupée) : moyenne 25.893 et variance 112.881 (écart type 10.625).

Question 2 (c) et (d) : le tracé est à faire par l'élève ; le corrigé donne le tableau des fréquences cumulées (bornes supérieures réelles 9.5, 14.5, ..., 49.5 car les longueurs sont arrondies au cm) et une figure modèle (PNG tracé par script, pas figure imprimée du sujet). Les quartiles sont lus aux fréquences cumulées 35 et 105 : lecture graphique $Q_1 \approx 17.8$, $Q_3 \approx 33.7$ ; interpolation linéaire $Q_1 = 17.74$, $Q_3 = 33.82$ ; l'écart interquartile attendu est donc $\approx 16$ cm (15.9 par lecture, 16.1 par interpolation).

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) State the modal class of this distribution of lengths.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The class widths are all equal (5 cm), so the modal class is the class with the largest frequency. The highest frequency is $25$, in the class $25 - 29$.

**The modal class is $25 - 29$ cm.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Calculate the mean and variance of the lengths of the leaves, to 3 decimal places.
(c) Construct the cumulative frequency table and draw the cumulative frequency curve for these data.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Lengths are given to the nearest cm, so the class $5 - 9$ really covers $4.5 \le \text{length} < 9.5$, and the class boundaries are $4.5,\ 9.5,\ 14.5, \ldots, 49.5$. A cumulative frequency is attached to each **upper** class boundary.

| Length less than (cm) | 4.5 | 9.5 | 14.5 | 19.5 | 24.5 | 29.5 | 34.5 | 39.5 | 44.5 | 49.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cumulative frequency | 0 | 11 | 24 | 41 | 61 | 86 | 108 | 124 | 136 | 140 |

**To draw the curve:** take the length (cm) on the horizontal axis, e.g. 1 cm for 5 cm from 4.5 to 50, and the cumulative frequency on the vertical axis, e.g. 1 cm for 20 from 0 to 140. Plot the ten points $(4.5, 0), (9.5, 11), (14.5, 24), \ldots, (49.5, 140)$ and join them with a smooth S-shaped curve (the ogive), which rises from $0$ at $4.5$ to $140$ at $49.5$.

![fig-1](gce-al-pm-statistics-2024-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_2_fig_1.png)

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) Use your curve to estimate the interquartile range.
questions.corrige_markdown:
With $n = 140$, the lower quartile is the value at cumulative frequency $\frac{140}{4} = 35$ and the upper quartile at $\frac{3 \times 140}{4} = 105$.

Reading the curve (dashed lines in the figure above): $Q_1 \approx 17.8$ cm and $Q_3 \approx 33.7$ cm.

Check by linear interpolation inside the classes containing 35 and 105:

$$Q_1 = 14.5 + \frac{35 - 24}{41 - 24} \times 5 = 17.7, \qquad Q_3 = 29.5 + \frac{105 - 86}{108 - 86} \times 5 = 33.8.$$

$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 \approx 33.7 - 17.8 = 15.9 \approx 16.$$

**The interquartile range is about $16$ cm** (any graphical estimate close to 16 is acceptable).
